page: Microsoft Azure NV12ads_A10_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for graphics-intensive desktop virtualization and lightweight machine learning inference. Built on the x86_64 architecture with AMD processors under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 12 dedicated vCPUs and a fractional NVIDIA A10 GPU allocation equivalent to one-third of a physical processor. This accelerator slice supplies 8 GB of dedicated video memory, providing hardware acceleration for display encoding, 3D rendering, and targeted tensor computing tasks.

System memory is configured at 110 GB, translating to 9.17 GB per vCPU. This elevated memory density supports data-heavy graphical applications and working datasets that exceed the requirements of standard compute-focused virtual machines. Complementing the processing subsystem is 387 GB of bundled local solid-state storage for swap space, temporary cache, and ephemeral runtime data, alongside integrated support for Azure Premium Storage.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the fractional GPU division, which prevents access to a full GPU core pipeline or larger VRAM configurations. In return, the instance delivers a cost-efficient resource profile by eliminating the need to pay for an entire dedicated GPU when running workloads that do not saturate full accelerator resources. It provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default, necessitating dedicated network routing or gateway provisioning for external access.

The hardware configuration is suitable for remote visualization, computer-aided design (CAD), virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI), video transcoding, interactive 3D rendering, and small-batch machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure NV12ads_A10_v5 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine engineered for visualization, virtual desktop infrastructure, and entry-level machine learning inference. Powered by an x86_64 AMD processor managed by Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 12 dedicated vCPUs and 110 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 9.17 GB per vCPU. Graphical acceleration is handled by a fractional one-third partition of an NVIDIA A10 GPU, supplying 8 GB of dedicated video memory. Local ephemeral capacity consists of a bundled 387 GB solid-state disk suitable for scratch files and caching, with support for Azure Premium Storage tiers. By sharing a physical GPU through hardware virtualization, this configuration delivers specialized acceleration without the resource overhead and operational expense of a full dedicated accelerator. The system is matched to remote CAD workflows, digital content creation, and modest AI inference pipelines.
